nonblocking_findings.issue: The text is bound to `regalim` identities (urn:x-opensiddur:text:siddur:regalim/musaf/text/veteerav, …/sheotekha) and reused for Rosh Hashanah. That isn't tied to this publication, and sharing it is fine if the canonical text really is the same. Separately, Veteerav and Birkat Kohanim are usually said only when the kohanim bless the congregation, and that depends on custom and on Israel vs. the diaspora. Neither record has a condition. If the printed source gives no condition, that's acceptable as a documentary encoding, but the order group should know about it.

The Musaf unit is bound to a canonical identity under the Shacharit path (shacharit/repetition/birkat_kohanim/birkat_kohanim). Reusing a text across services is fine. But the path is under Shacharit and is the same for the introduction and the blessing, which may mislead whoever uses it next. Consider a neutral shared identity.

If that URN is the weekday blessing's identity, this binding merges two separate texts. Please confirm that the URN is reserved for the Rosh Hashanah Shofarot text.
